records.source: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν εἶπεν ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λέγων·
records.gloss: And answering, the Jesus again spoke in parables to them, saying:
pieces: Once more Jesus answered them by speaking in parables:

L.1: And answering, Jesus again spoke to them in parables, saying,

R.1: Jesus answered them again by telling stories. He told this one:

decisions.choice: answering: responding to the situation, the leaders' wish to arrest him (21:45-46)
decisions.reason: No one has asked a question. The word often means simply "spoke up" in reply to what had happened.

decisions.choice: in parables: by way of parables, the manner of his teaching
decisions.reason: Only one parable follows. The plural describes how he taught, as in 13:3 and 22:1.

decisions.choice: telling stories; He told this one
decisions.reason: Readable says what parables are and introduces the one story that follows.

records.heading: The king's wedding banquet

records.source: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ, ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Has become like the kingdom of the heavens to a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for the son of him.
pieces: "What happens in the kingdom of heaven can be compared to this: a king prepared a wedding banquet for his son.

L.2: "The kingdom of the heavens has become like a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for his son.

R.2: "The kingdom of heaven is like this. A king gave a big wedding party for his son.

decisions.choice: has become like: the kingdom is compared to the whole story that follows
alternatives: the kingdom is like the king himself
decisions.reason: The same form begins the parables of 13:24 and 18:23. The point lies in the events of the story, not in the king alone.

decisions.choice: wedding feast: the celebration of a marriage, which could last several days
decisions.reason: The plural word names the wedding festivities. A king's feast for his son was the greatest celebration a city could see.

decisions.choice: the king and his son: God and Jesus, as in the vineyard owner's son (21:37)
alternatives: a story with no figure for God
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God's coming rule as a feast (Isaiah 25:6), and Jesus has just told of a father who sent his son (21:37). The parable's figures still remain figures in a story.

decisions.choice: a man, a king
decisions.reason: The Greek says "a man, a king", a common way of introducing a character. Balanced and Readable say "a king".

decisions.choice: his son: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The king is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span, as with the bridegroom in 9:15.

records.source: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν.
records.gloss: And he sent the slaves of him to call those having been invited to the wedding feast, and not they were willing to come.
pieces: He sent his servants to summon the guests who had already been invited, but they refused to come.

L.3: And he sent his slaves to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, and they were not willing to come.

R.3: He sent his servants to tell the invited guests to come to the party. But they would not come.

decisions.choice: two invitations: one sent ahead of time, then a call when the feast was ready
alternatives: a first invitation on the day
decisions.reason: Guests were invited in advance and then summoned when the meal was ready (compare Esther 5:8; 6:14). These guests had already accepted the first invitation.

decisions.choice: slaves: persons owned by the king and sent on his business
decisions.reason: The word names a slave (8:9; 10:24). A king's slaves could carry his messages with his authority.

decisions.choice: the slaves sent: God's messengers to Israel
decisions.reason: As in the parable of the tenants (21:34-36), the slaves sent and mistreated recall the prophets God sent to his people (23:34-37).

decisions.choice: they were not willing: they kept refusing
decisions.reason: The verb means to want or be willing. The guests chose not to come.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων· Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ἡτοίμακα, οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα, καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα· δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
records.gloss: Again he sent other slaves, saying, Say to those having been invited, Behold, the dinner of me I have prepared, the oxen of me and the fatlings having been slaughtered, and all things ready; come to the wedding feast.
pieces: So he sent more servants with this message: 'Tell the guests, "See, my banquet is prepared. My bulls and my fattened calves have been slaughtered. Everything is ready, so come to the wedding."'

L.4: Again he sent other slaves, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited, "Look, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything [is] ready. Come to the wedding feast."'

R.4: Then the king sent some other servants. He told them, 'Say to the guests, "The meal is ready! I have killed my best cattle for the food. Everything is ready. Come to the wedding party!"'

decisions.choice: dinner: the first meal of the feast, eaten about midday
decisions.reason: The word names the morning or midday meal. Here it opens the wedding celebration.

decisions.choice: oxen and fattened animals: a lavish feast
decisions.reason: Meat was rare for most people. Slaughtering oxen and stall-fed animals showed a royal feast with no expense spared.

decisions.choice: look (L); see (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names the king so the reader keeps track of who is speaking.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον, ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν, ὃς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: But having paid no attention, they went away, one to the own field, another to the business of him;
pieces: The guests did not care. They went off, one to his farm and another to his trade.

L.5: But paying no attention, they went off, one to his own field, another to his business.

R.5: But the guests did not care. One went off to work in his field. Another went to his business.

decisions.choice: paying no attention: treating the invitation as unimportant
decisions.reason: The verb means to neglect or make light of something. They heard and did not care.

decisions.choice: business: trade, buying and selling
decisions.reason: The word names commerce. Ordinary work mattered more to them than the king's feast.

decisions.choice: the guests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who went off.

records.source: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.
records.gloss: And the rest, having seized the slaves of him, mistreated and killed [them].
pieces: The rest laid hands on the king's servants, abused them, and killed them.

L.6: And the rest seized his slaves, mistreated [them], and killed [them].

R.6: The rest of the guests grabbed the king's servants. They hurt them and killed them.

decisions.choice: mistreated: treated with insult and violence
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat someone with outrage and contempt. It can include beating.

decisions.choice: the slaves killed: as the tenants did in 21:35-36
alternatives: a new detail with no echo
decisions.reason: The parable repeats the pattern of the vineyard story and of Israel's treatment of the prophets (23:37).

decisions.choice: the king's; of the guests (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whose servants these were and who the rest were.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὠργίσθη, καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν.
records.gloss: The and king was angry, and having sent the armies of him he destroyed the murderers those and the city of them burned.
pieces: The king was furious. He sent his troops, wiped out those murderers, and set their city on fire.

L.7: But the king was angry, and sending his armies he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.

R.7: The king became very angry. He sent his soldiers to kill those murderers and burn down their city.

decisions.choice: armies: troops, soldiers
decisions.reason: The plural word means bodies of soldiers.

decisions.choice: burned their city: the judgment that falls on those who refused the king
alternatives: a direct prediction of the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70
decisions.reason: Burning a rebel city was a common act of war and a picture the prophets use for judgment (Isaiah 1:7). Many readers see a pointer to the destruction of Jerusalem (compare 23:38; 24:2); the parable does not name the city.

records.source: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι·
records.gloss: Then he says to the slaves of him, The indeed wedding feast ready is, but those having been invited were not worthy;
pieces: Then he told his servants, 'The wedding is ready, but the guests I invited did not deserve to come.

L.8: Then he says to his slaves, 'The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.

R.8: Then the king said to his servants, 'The wedding party is ready. But the people I invited did not deserve to come.

decisions.choice: not worthy: they showed themselves unfit by refusing
decisions.reason: Their refusal and violence proved them unworthy of the honor (compare 10:11-13).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, καὶ ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.
records.gloss: Go therefore to the thoroughfares of the highways, and as many as you find invite to the wedding feast.
pieces: So go out to where the roads leave the city, and invite to the wedding anyone you come across.'

L.9: Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and as many as you find, invite to the wedding feast.'

R.9: So go out to the main roads. Invite everyone you find to come to the wedding party.'

decisions.choice: the outlets of the roads: where the city streets run out into the country roads
alternatives: the main crossroads in the city
decisions.reason: The word names a way out or a place where roads branch. Either way, it is where many travelers would be found.

decisions.choice: as many as you find: an invitation open to all
decisions.reason: The king no longer asks who the guests are. The parable echoes 8:11, where many come from east and west.

decisions.choice: where the roads leave the city
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly what the phrase describes.

records.source: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας οὓς εὗρον, πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς· καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων.
records.gloss: And having gone out, those slaves into the highways gathered all whom they found, both evil and good; and was filled the wedding feast with those reclining.
pieces: The servants went out into the streets and brought in everyone they could find, bad and good alike, and the wedding feast was crowded with guests.

L.10: And those slaves went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both evil and good; and the wedding feast was filled with those reclining [at table].

R.10: So the servants went out into the roads. They brought in all the people they could find, both bad people and good people. Soon the wedding party was full of guests.

decisions.choice: evil and good: the invitation goes to all, whatever their lives
decisions.reason: Bad and good are gathered alike. The sorting comes later, as in the net of 13:47-48 and here in 22:11-13.

decisions.choice: reclining: guests at a feast lay on couches around the table
decisions.reason: As in 8:11 and 9:10, guests at a banquet reclined.

decisions.choice: the wedding feast, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the wedding hall, the reading of other manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "the wedding hall" here. The sense is the same: the place of the feast was full. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου·
records.gloss: Having entered then the king to see those reclining, he saw there a man not clothed in clothing of wedding;
pieces: The king came in to look over his guests, and among them he saw a man who had not put on clothes for a wedding.

L.11: But when the king came in to look at those reclining [at table], he saw there a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.

R.11: Then the king came in to meet the guests. He saw one man there who was not dressed for a wedding.

decisions.choice: wedding clothes: clean, festive clothing fit for the occasion
alternatives: clothing given out by the host
decisions.reason: Guests were expected to come in clean clothes worthy of the feast. Whether the host supplied them is not stated and cannot be shown from the customs of the time.

decisions.choice: the wedding clothes: a life that fits the invitation
alternatives: a righteousness given as a gift
decisions.reason: The parable does not explain the garment. In Matthew the kingdom calls for a righteousness that goes beyond outward show (5:20; 7:21) and for fruit fitting repentance (3:8). Others read it as faith, or as a gift from the host.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου;
records.gloss: And he says to him, Friend, how did you enter here not having clothing of wedding?
pieces: He said to him, 'Friend, how is it that you came in here with no wedding clothes on?'

L.12: And he says to him, 'Friend, how did you come in here without having wedding clothes?'

R.12: The king said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here? You are not dressed for a wedding.'

decisions.choice: friend: a polite address, here with a note of reproach
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this address for someone in the wrong: the grumbling worker (20:13) and Judas (26:50).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: a question and a statement
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question to keep the sentences short.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη.
records.gloss: He but was speechless.
pieces: The man had nothing to say.

R.12: The man did not know what to say.

decisions.choice: speechless: silenced, with no excuse to give
decisions.reason: The verb means to be muzzled. The same word is used of the Sadducees in 22:34.

records.source: τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τοῖς διακόνοις· Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
records.gloss: Then the king said to the servants, Having bound of him feet and hands, throw out him into the darkness the outer; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
pieces: The king then gave orders to his attendants: 'Bind his hands and feet and throw him out into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth.'

L.13: Then the king said to the servants, 'Bind his feet and hands and throw him out into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'

R.13: Then the king said to his attendants, 'Tie up this man's hands and feet. Throw him outside into the dark. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'

decisions.choice: the outer darkness, weeping and gnashing of teeth: exclusion and anguish
alternatives: a literal room outside the hall
decisions.reason: As in 8:12, the darkness outside the lighted hall pictures being shut out of the kingdom, and grinding the teeth shows anguish. The wording is kept the same as in 8:12 at each level.

decisions.choice: servants: attendants who wait at table
alternatives: the same slaves who invited the guests
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the slaves of 22:3-10. In the parable of the weeds, angels carry out the final sorting (13:41-42).

decisions.choice: there will be weeping: the king's words, which also speak of the final judgment
alternatives: a comment by Jesus outside the story
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuation keeps the clause in the king's sentence. The words are Jesus's own phrase for final judgment (8:12; 13:42), so the story and its meaning meet here.

decisions.choice: servants (L); attendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the one in 22:3-10, which Literal renders "slaves" and Balanced and Readable "servants". To keep the two groups apart, Literal says "servants" here and Balanced and Readable "attendants".

records.source: πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.
records.gloss: Many for are called, few but chosen.
pieces: For the invited are many, but the chosen are few."

L.14: For many are called, but few [are] chosen."

R.14: God invites many people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses only a few."

decisions.choice: called: invited
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "invited" in 22:3-9. Many receive the king's invitation.

decisions.choice: chosen: those whom God accepts at the feast
decisions.reason: The saying sums up the parable. Many were invited, yet the first guests refused and one guest was thrown out. The chosen are those who come and are found fit, by God's choice.

decisions.choice: God invites; he chooses
alternatives: many are called, few are chosen
decisions.reason: The passive words imply that God is the one who calls and chooses. Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the invited are many, the chosen are few
alternatives: many are invited, few are chosen
decisions.reason: Balanced sets the two groups side by side as the Greek does, with the numbers last for emphasis.

records.source: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.
records.gloss: Then having gone, the Pharisees took counsel how him they might trap in a word.
pieces: Then the Pharisees went off and plotted how they could catch Jesus out by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own words.

L.15: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in [what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said].

R.15: Then the Pharisees went away and made plans. They wanted to trick Jesus into saying something wrong.

decisions.choice: trap: catch, as a hunter snares an animal
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a snare. They wanted a statement they could use against him.

decisions.choice: took counsel: made a plan together
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 12:14, when the Pharisees plot to destroy Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: A question about paying Caesar

records.source: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·
records.gloss: And they send to him the disciples of them with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that true you are and the way of God in truth you teach, and not it is a care to you about no one, not for you look at face of men;
pieces: They sent their own disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along with the Herodians. "Teacher," they said, "we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are truthful and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach God's way in keeping with the truth. No one's opinion moves {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not judge people by their rank.

L.16: And they send their disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are true and teach the way of God in truth, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not care about anyone, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not look at [the] face of {{gender:people|men}}.

R.16: They sent some of their followers to Jesus, together with some men who supported King Herod's family. They said, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are honest. We know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach the truth about the way God wants people to live. You are not afraid of anyone, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treat important people the same as everyone else.

decisions.choice: the Herodians: supporters of Herod's family, who ruled under Rome
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas ruled Galilee with Rome's approval. His supporters would favor the tax; many Pharisees resented it. The two groups were unlikely allies (Mark 3:6).

decisions.choice: look at the face of men: show favor because of a person's rank or appearance
decisions.reason: The law forbids judging by a person's standing (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 1:17). They praise Jesus for fearing no one, hoping he will answer rashly.

decisions.choice: true, in truth: honest, teaching what is really God's way
decisions.reason: Their words are flattery meant to set a trap (22:15, 18), yet what they say about Jesus is so.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: men who supported King Herod's family; the truth about the way God wants people to live
alternatives: the Herodians; the way of God in truth
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Herodians were and what "the way of God" means.

decisions.choice: truthful (B); honest (R)
decisions.reason: The adjective describes a person who speaks the truth. The noun "truth" later in the verse stays "truth" at every level.

records.source: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;
records.gloss: Tell therefore us what to you seems: is it lawful to give poll tax to Caesar or not?
pieces: So give us {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} opinion. Does the law permit paying the head tax to Caesar, or not?"

L.17: Tell us then, what do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think? Is it lawful to give [the] poll tax to Caesar, or not?"

R.17: So tell us what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think. Does God's law allow us to pay taxes to Caesar, the Roman emperor? Or should we refuse?"

decisions.choice: poll tax: a yearly tax on each person, paid to Rome
decisions.reason: Rome took a tax on each person in Judea, paid in Roman coin. Many Jews hated it as a sign of foreign rule; a revolt broke out over it in AD 6 (Acts 5:37).

decisions.choice: Caesar: the Roman emperor, at this time Tiberius
decisions.reason: Caesar was the family name of the first emperors and became their title.

decisions.choice: is it lawful: allowed by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The question is whether paying a pagan ruler is right for God's people. "Yes" would anger the crowds; "no" would be rebellion against Rome.

decisions.choice: head tax (B); taxes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain word for a tax on each person. Readable keeps it general and explains Caesar.

decisions.choice: Or should we refuse?
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the other half of the question.

records.source: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Τί με πειράζετε, ὑποκριταί;
records.gloss: Having known however Jesus the malice of them, said, Why me do you test, hypocrites?
pieces: Jesus was aware of their malice. "You hypocrites," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "why are you putting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to the test?

L.18: But Jesus, knowing their malice, said, "Why are you testing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, hypocrites?

R.18: But Jesus knew they were trying to do something evil. He said, "You are only pretending to be good! Why are you trying to trap {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: test: try to catch him out
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the Pharisees' questions in 16:1, 19:3 and 22:35, and of the devil in 4:1.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people whose words hide their real aims
decisions.reason: Their praise in 22:16 covered a trap. The word first meant an actor.

decisions.choice: You are only pretending to be good
decisions.reason: As in 7:5, Readable says what a hypocrite does.

records.source: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου.
records.gloss: Show me the coin of the tax.
pieces: Show {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the coin that pays the tax."

L.19: Show {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the coin for the poll tax."

R.19: Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} see one of the coins you use to pay the tax."

decisions.choice: the coin of the tax: the Roman silver coin the tax had to be paid in
decisions.reason: The poll tax was paid in Roman money, the denarius. Jesus asks them to produce one; he does not take it from his own purse.

records.source: οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον.
records.gloss: And they brought to him a denarius.
pieces: They brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} {{units:a silver coin worth a day's wage|a denarius}}.

R.19: They brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} {{units:a silver coin, the kind a worker earns in a day|a denarius}}.

decisions.choice: denarius: a Roman silver coin, a day's wage for a laborer
decisions.reason: A vineyard worker is paid a denarius for a day's work in 20:2.

decisions.choice: units setting for the denarius
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman coin's name. Balanced and Readable describe it, with denarius as the setting's alternative.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;
records.gloss: And he says to them, Whose image this and the inscription?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Whose portrait is this? And whose title is written on it?"

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Whose image [is] this, and [whose] inscription?"

R.20: Jesus asked them, "Whose picture is on this coin? Whose name is written on it?"

decisions.choice: image and inscription: the emperor's head and his titles
decisions.reason: The denarius of Tiberius bore his head and an inscription naming him son of the divine Augustus. Many Jews found such coins offensive.

decisions.choice: image: perhaps an echo of people made in God's image (Genesis 1:27)
decisions.reason: The word is the one the Greek Old Testament uses in Genesis 1:26-27. If the coin bearing Caesar's image belongs to Caesar, what bears God's image belongs to God. Jesus does not say this outright.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος.
records.gloss: They say to him, Caesar's.
pieces: "Caesar's," they answered.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.
records.gloss: Then he says to them, Give back therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar and the things of God to God.
pieces: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Then pay Caesar what you owe Caesar, and pay God what you owe God."

L.21: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Give back then the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God."

R.21: Jesus said to them, "So pay back to Caesar what is his. And pay back to God what is God's."

decisions.choice: give back: pay what is owed
decisions.reason: The verb differs from "give" in their question (22:17). It means to pay back a debt. The coin already belongs to Caesar.

decisions.choice: the things of God: all that belongs to God, the people themselves included
decisions.reason: The answer neither forbids the tax nor puts Caesar on God's level. If the coin bears Caesar's image, people bear God's (Genesis 1:27), and owe him themselves. The second half has the greater weight.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: pay what you owe (B); pay back (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that this is a debt being paid.

records.source: καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν, καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν.
records.gloss: And having heard they marveled, and having left him they went away.
pieces: His answer astonished them, and they went off and left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone.

L.22: And hearing [this], they marveled, and they left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and went away.

R.22: They were amazed at what Jesus said. So they left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and went away.

decisions.choice: marveled: were amazed, though not won over
decisions.reason: They have no reply, so they leave. Amazement in Matthew does not always mean belief (8:27; 27:14).

records.source: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι, λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν, καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα, ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: On that day came to him Sadducees, saying not to be a resurrection, and they questioned him, \v 24 saying, Teacher, Moses said, If anyone should die not having children, will marry the brother of him the wife of him and will raise up offspring for the brother of him.
pieces: That same day some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses gave this rule: 'If a man dies and leaves no children, his brother is to take the widow as his wife and so give his dead brother descendants.'

L.23: On that day Sadducees came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying that there is no resurrection, and they questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.24: saying, "Teacher, Moses said, 'If anyone dies having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.'

R.23: That same day some Sadducees came to Jesus. The Sadducees taught that dead people do not rise to life again. They asked Jesus a question.
R.24: They said, "Teacher, Moses wrote in the law, 'If a man dies without children, his brother must marry the dead man's wife. Then their children will count as the children of the brother who died.'

decisions.choice: Sadducees: a party of priests and leading families
decisions.reason: They held to the written law and rejected teachings not found there. They denied the resurrection and the existence of angels and spirits (Acts 23:8).

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 25:5-6: a brother marries the widow to give the dead man an heir
alternatives: a rule of the Sadducees' own
decisions.reason: The law kept a man's name and land in his family through his brother's children. The words "raise up offspring for his brother" echo Genesis 38:8.

decisions.choice: saying, without the article, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the ones who say, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add the article, so that the phrase describes the Sadducees as those who deny the resurrection. Without it, they come saying so. The sense is much the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: brother: no gender span
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a particular man's male brother who marries the widow, so the word takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: wrote in the law; their children will count as the children of the brother who died
alternatives: said; raise up offspring for his brother
decisions.reason: Readable says where Moses said it and explains what raising up offspring for a brother meant.

records.heading: Marriage and the resurrection

records.source: ἦσαν δὲ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν, καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: There were now among us seven brothers; and the first having married died, and not having offspring he left the wife of him to the brother of him;
pieces: There were seven brothers in our community. The first one married and died, and because he had no children, his widow went to his brother.

L.25: Now there were seven brothers among us; and the first married and died, and having no offspring he left his wife to his brother.

R.25: There were seven brothers who lived near us. The first brother got married, but he died. He had no children, so his brother married his wife.

decisions.choice: among us: told as a real case
decisions.reason: They present it as something that happened. It may be a case invented to make belief in the resurrection look foolish.

decisions.choice: offspring: children
decisions.reason: The word means seed and is often used for descendants.

records.source: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος, ἕως τῶν ἑπτά·
records.gloss: Likewise also the second and the third, until the seven;
pieces: The same thing happened to the second brother, and the third, and so on through all seven.

L.26: Likewise also the second and the third, up to the seventh.

R.26: The same thing happened to the second brother and the third brother. It happened to all seven of them.

decisions.choice: up to the seventh: each of the seven in turn
decisions.reason: The phrase means the pattern went on through all seven brothers.

records.source: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἡ γυνή.
records.gloss: Last then of all died the woman.
pieces: Finally, after them all, the woman died.

L.27: And last of all the woman died.

R.27: Last of all, the woman died too.

records.source: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οὖν τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή;
records.gloss: In the resurrection therefore of which of the seven will she be wife?
pieces: So when the dead are raised, which of the seven will have her as his wife?

L.28: In the resurrection, then, of which of the seven will she be [the] wife?

R.28: So when people rise from death, which of the seven brothers will she be married to?

decisions.choice: in the resurrection: when the dead are raised at the last day
decisions.reason: The phrase names the time when God raises the dead (Daniel 12:2). The Sadducees speak of it to mock it.

decisions.choice: when the dead are raised (B); when people rise from death (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the resurrection is.

records.source: πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν.
records.gloss: All for had her.
pieces: All of them were married to her."

R.28: All seven of them had been her husband."

decisions.choice: had her: had her as a wife
decisions.reason: To have a woman means to be married to her (14:4).

records.source: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: Answering then Jesus said to them, You err not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God;
pieces: Jesus replied, "You have gone astray, because you understand neither the Scriptures nor God's power.

L.29: But Jesus answered them, "You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures or the power of God.

R.29: Jesus answered them, "You are wrong! You do not understand what the Scriptures say. And you do not know how powerful God is.

decisions.choice: you are mistaken: you have wandered from the truth
decisions.reason: The verb means to go astray. It can be passive, "you are led astray", but the sense here is that they are in error.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures and the power of God: both answered in what follows
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of God's power in 22:30, where the raised do not marry, and of the Scriptures in 22:31-32.

records.source: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἄγγελοι θεοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν·
records.gloss: In for the resurrection neither do they marry nor are given in marriage, but like angels of God in heaven they are.
pieces: For once the dead are raised, men no longer take wives and women are no longer given as brides; they are like the angels of God in heaven.

L.30: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like angels of God in heaven.

R.30: After people rise from death, they do not get married. They are like God's angels in heaven.

decisions.choice: marry and are given in marriage: men took wives, and fathers gave their daughters
alternatives: two names for the same act
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe the man's part and the bride's. Neither happens after the resurrection.

decisions.choice: like angels: in not marrying, not in becoming angels
decisions.reason: Raised people do not die (Luke 20:36), so marriage to provide heirs is no longer needed. Jesus also affirms the angels the Sadducees denied (Acts 23:8).

decisions.choice: of God, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: like angels in heaven, the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "of God", and others have "angels of God". The meaning does not change. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: men no longer take wives and women are no longer given as brides
alternatives: they neither marry nor are given in marriage
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the two sides the verbs describe.

records.source: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγοντος·
records.gloss: Concerning now the resurrection of the dead, not have you read what was spoken to you by God, saying,
pieces: As for the dead being raised, have you not read what God said to you:

L.31: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying,

R.31: And about dead people rising to life: have you not read what God told you? He said,

decisions.choice: spoken to you by God: God's word to Moses speaks to them too
decisions.reason: Scripture is God speaking to each generation that reads it, the Sadducees included.

decisions.choice: have you not read: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: As in 12:3, Jesus asks whether they have understood what they read. The Sadducees held the books of Moses in the highest honor.

decisions.choice: He said
decisions.reason: Readable ends the question and begins a new sentence for God's words. At the start of a sentence the pronoun is capitalized either way.

records.source: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ;
records.gloss: I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?
pieces: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?

L.32: 'I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'?

R.32: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:6: God speaks to Moses from the bush
decisions.reason: God named himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob centuries after their deaths (also Exodus 3:15-16). Jesus quotes the law of Moses, which the Sadducees accepted.

decisions.choice: I am: God is still their God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Exodus 3:6 has no verb; the argument rests on God calling himself their God long after they died. A God of the living does not bind himself to those who have ceased to be.

decisions.choice: a question mark at the end: the quotation completes the question of 22:31
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates the whole of 22:31-32a as one question.

decisions.choice: statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable made 22:31 a complete question, so the quotation ends as a statement.

records.source: οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων.
records.gloss: Not is he the God of dead but of living.
pieces: He is God not of the dead but of the living."

L.32: He is not the God of [the] dead but of [the] living."

R.32: God is not the God of people who are dead. He is the God of people who are alive."

decisions.choice: God of the living: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob live to God and will be raised
alternatives: the patriarchs are dead and gone
decisions.reason: Because God is still their God, death has not ended them. Jesus draws from this that God will raise the dead.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God to make the subject clear.

records.source: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having heard, the crowds were astonished at the teaching of him.
pieces: His teaching amazed the crowds who heard it.

L.33: And hearing [it], the crowds were astounded at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.

R.33: The people who heard this were amazed at what Jesus taught.

decisions.choice: astounded: struck with amazement
decisions.reason: As at the end of the Sermon on the Mount (7:28), the crowds are amazed at his teaching.

records.source: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
records.gloss: The but Pharisees having heard that he had silenced the Sadducees were gathered together at the same.
pieces: The Pharisees heard that Jesus had put the Sadducees to silence, and they came together in one place.

L.34: But the Pharisees, hearing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had silenced the Sadducees, gathered together.

R.34: The Pharisees heard that Jesus had answered the Sadducees so well that they could say nothing more. So the Pharisees met together.

decisions.choice: silenced: left with nothing to say
decisions.reason: The verb means to muzzle. It is used of the guest without wedding clothes (22:12).

decisions.choice: gathered together: perhaps an echo of Psalm 2:2
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament of Psalm 2:2 the rulers are "gathered together" against the LORD and his anointed, in the same words. Whether Matthew intends the echo is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: The command that ranks highest

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων αὐτόν·
records.gloss: And questioned one of them, a lawyer, testing him:
pieces: One of their number, a man trained in the law, put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:

L.35: And one of them, a lawyer, questioned [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:

R.35: One of them knew the law of Moses very well. He wanted to test Jesus, so he asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a question.

decisions.choice: lawyer: an expert in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word names a scholar of the law, much like a scribe. It appears only here in Matthew.

decisions.choice: testing: putting him to a test
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 22:18. In Matthew the Pharisees' testing is meant to catch Jesus out (16:1; 19:3).

decisions.choice: a lawyer, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: one of them, without "a lawyer", the reading of a few witnesses
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts and early translations lack the word, and some think it was added from Luke 10:25. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man trained in the law (B); knew the law of Moses very well (R)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests a courtroom. Balanced and Readable say what kind of expert he was.

records.source: Διδάσκαλε, ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ;
records.gloss: Teacher, which commandment great in the law?
pieces: "Teacher, which commandment in the law ranks highest?"

L.36: "Teacher, which commandment [is] great in the law?"

R.36: "Teacher, which command in the law of Moses is the most important?"

decisions.choice: great: the greatest
decisions.reason: The plain form "great" often has the force of "greatest" in the Greek of the time.

decisions.choice: a common question: which command carries the most weight
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers discussed heavier and lighter commands (compare 23:23). Later tradition counted 613 commands in the law.

decisions.choice: ranks highest (B); most important (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the plain form.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου·
records.gloss: He and said to him, You shall love Lord the God of you with all the heart of you and with all the soul of you and with all the mind of you;
pieces: Jesus answered him, "'Love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, and with your whole mind.'

L.37: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "'You shall love [the] Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.'

R.37: Jesus answered, "'Love the Lord your God with all of your heart. Love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all of your soul and with all of your mind.'

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:5, part of the Shema
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 6:4-9 was recited daily by devout Jews. Deuteronomy has heart, soul and strength; Matthew has mind in place of strength, and Mark 12:30 has all four.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 6:5 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". As in 4:7 and 4:10.

decisions.choice: heart, soul and mind: the whole person
alternatives: three separate parts of a person
decisions.reason: Heart is the inner self, soul is life itself, and mind is thought and understanding. Together they mean love with all one is.

decisions.choice: Love (B, R)
decisions.reason: The future tense gives a command. Balanced and Readable use the plain command form, as in 5:43.

decisions.choice: Love him
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb to keep the sentences short.

records.source: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη ἐντολή.
records.gloss: This is the great and first commandment.
pieces: This command is the great one, the first of all.

L.38: This is the great and first commandment.

R.38: This is the most important command. It comes first.

decisions.choice: first: first in rank
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the question of 22:36. Love for God is the command over all the others.

records.source: Δευτέρα δὲ ὁμοία αὐτῇ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
records.gloss: Second and like it: You shall love the neighbor of you as yourself.
pieces: A second command is of the same kind: 'Love your neighbor as you love yourself.'

L.39: And [the] second [is] like it: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'

R.39: The second command is like the first one. It says, 'Love other people as much as you love yourself.'

decisions.choice: Leviticus 19:18: love your neighbor
decisions.reason: Jesus quoted it in 5:43 and 19:19. In Leviticus the neighbor is a fellow Israelite; Jesus extends love even to enemies (5:44).

decisions.choice: like it: of the same kind, also a command to love
decisions.reason: Both commands begin with the same verb. Love for neighbor flows from love for God and is bound to it.

decisions.choice: other people
decisions.reason: "Neighbor" can sound like someone who lives next door. Readable says the command covers other people.

records.source: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
records.gloss: On these two commandments the whole law hangs and the prophets.
pieces: The whole of the law, and the prophets as well, hangs on these two commands."

L.40: On these two commandments the whole law hangs, and the prophets."

R.40: All of the law of Moses and all the teachings of the prophets depend on these two commands."

decisions.choice: hangs: depends on, as a door hangs on its hinge
alternatives: is summed up and replaced by
decisions.reason: The two commands do not cancel the others. All the others rest on them.

decisions.choice: the law and the prophets: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: As in 5:17 and 7:12, where the golden rule is called "the law and the prophets".

decisions.choice: the law of Moses, the teachings of the prophets
decisions.reason: As in 5:17 and 7:12.

records.source: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ;
records.gloss: Having been gathered now the Pharisees, questioned them the Jesus \v 42 saying, What to you seems concerning the Christ?
pieces: While the Pharisees were still gathered there, Jesus put a question to them:
"What is your view of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

L.41: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
L.42: saying, "What do you think about the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

R.41: While the Pharisees were still together, Jesus asked them,
R.42: "What do you think about the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the one God promised to send?

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king they expected
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title: the anointed one God promised (2:4; 16:16).

decisions.choice: Jesus questioned them: now he asks the question
decisions.reason: After three tests from his opponents (22:15-40), Jesus asks his own.

decisions.choice: the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means.

records.heading: Whose son is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

records.source: τίνος υἱός ἐστιν;
records.gloss: Of whom son is he?
pieces: Whose son is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}?"

decisions.choice: son: descendant
alternatives: a child of the next generation
decisions.reason: "Son of" often means descendant, as in 1:1.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun span for the Christ
decisions.reason: The question is about the Messiah, whom Matthew presents as Jesus himself, so pronouns for him take the setting here and in 22:43-45.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τοῦ Δαυίδ.
records.gloss: They say to him, Of David.
pieces: "David's," they answered.

R.42: They answered, "He is the son of David."

decisions.choice: of David: the expected king from David's line
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last for ever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). "Son of David" was a title for the coming king (9:27; 21:9).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πῶς οὖν Δαυὶδ ἐν πνεύματι καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον λέγων·
records.gloss: He says to them, How then David in spirit calls him Lord, saying,
pieces: He asked them, "Why then does David, moved by the Spirit, give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the title Lord? For David says,

L.43: He says to them, "How then does David in [the] Spirit call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Lord, saying,

R.43: Jesus said to them, "Then why does David call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 'Lord'? The Holy Spirit led David to write,

decisions.choice: in spirit: by the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: David spoke as the Spirit led him (2 Samuel 23:2). His words carry God's authority.

decisions.choice: calls him Lord: a father would not call his own descendant Lord
decisions.reason: Jesus and the Pharisees agree that David wrote the psalm. A forefather was greater than his descendants, so David's "Lord" must be more than his son.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: two sentences (B, R)
alternatives: one question that runs on into the psalm
decisions.reason: In the Greek the question runs through the quotation of 22:44. Balanced and Readable end the question first and then quote the psalm.

records.source: Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου;
records.gloss: Said the Lord to the Lord of me, Sit at right of me until I put the enemies of you under the feet of you?
pieces: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Take {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} seat at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand until I have put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies beneath {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'

L.44: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right [hand], until I put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet"'?

R.44: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side, the place of honor, until I defeat {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies and put them under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'

decisions.choice: Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: The psalm is headed "of David". It is the Old Testament verse the New Testament quotes most often of Jesus (26:64; Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13).

decisions.choice: the Lord ... my Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew, and David's master
decisions.reason: In Psalm 110:1 the first "Lord" is God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". "My Lord" is a different Hebrew word, used of a master or king. In Greek both are "Lord".

decisions.choice: at my right hand: the place of highest honor and shared rule
decisions.reason: The one seated at a king's right hand shared his authority (1 Kings 2:19).

decisions.choice: under, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a footstool for, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet", the wording of the psalm in the Greek Old Testament. The SBLGNT reads "under your feet", as in Mark 12:36. The sense is the same: complete defeat of his enemies. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: spans on God's "my" and on "your" for David's Lord; none on David's "my"
decisions.reason: God speaks to the Messiah, so both their pronouns take the setting. "My Lord" is David's own word.

decisions.choice: the place of honor; defeat
alternatives: at my right; put under your feet
decisions.reason: Readable explains the right hand and what putting enemies under the feet means.

records.source: εἰ οὖν Δαυὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον, πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν;
records.gloss: If therefore David calls him Lord, how son of him is he?
pieces: So if David calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 'Lord', how can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be David's son?"

L.45: If then David calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Lord, how is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} his son?"

R.45: David calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 'Lord.' So how can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be David's son?"

decisions.choice: the Messiah is David's son and more: David's Lord
alternatives: the Messiah is not descended from David
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny that the Messiah descends from David (1:1; 21:9). He shows that the title says too little. Matthew has shown that he is the Son of God (3:17; 16:16).

decisions.choice: David's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David so that "his" is not taken to mean God.

records.source: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ λόγον, οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπ’ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι.
records.gloss: And no one was able to answer him a word, nor dared anyone from that day to question him any longer.
pieces: None of them could give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} any answer at all. And after that day no one was bold enough to put another question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.46: And no one was able to answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} any longer.

R.46: No one could answer Jesus at all. And from that day on, no one was brave enough to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} any more questions.

decisions.choice: from that day: the end of the questions begun in 21:23
decisions.reason: The leaders' challenges in the temple end here. In chapter 23 Jesus speaks against them.
